Class TrainingSession

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.client.Trainer
dev.swordai.client.TrainingSession
All Implemented Interfaces:
AgentSession
public final class TrainingSession extends Trainer
Training on the screen: the agent plays the user's own character and sees the frames the game draws. One run, from /swordai train (or play / selftest) until it stops, driven once per client tick. What is trained, and how, is Trainer's; this class is the body.

    • viewYawLag

      public float viewYawLag(float partialTick)
      The player's rotation jumps once a tick; the picture should not. While a frame is drawn part-way through a tick, the view is held back by the part of this tick's turn that is still to come, so on screen the camera sweeps at an even speed and arrives exactly as the next tick begins.

    • waitForFrames

      private void waitForFrames()
      The agent cannot play blind. If the game stops delivering new frames (which a hidden window should not cause, but a driver or the system might), the episode is cut and the session waits here until frames flow again, instead of learning from a frozen picture.

    • judgesCopyFights

      boolean judgesCopyFights()
      On the screen no fight against a copy is on equal terms. The user's character sees the copy as a player sees another, a tick or more late, and its clicks reach the server a tick late; the copy is a fake player on the server and has neither delay. After two hours of it the fighter won one such fight in five against a copy it then beat four times in five without the screen. Counted, those fights would never let it take the copy's place, and at one win in ten self-play would throw away what it had learned on the screen and start again from the copy.
      Overrides:
      judgesCopyFights in class Trainer

    • slowDownIfBehind

      private void slowDownIfBehind()
      Faster than real time only works while every decision still gets a fresh frame and the server still fits a tick into its shorter time. If either fails, the fights the agent learns from are no longer the game's, so the speed comes down a step, by itself.
